items.headline: DEA says fentanyl remains Colorado's top drug threat after Aurora overdose leaves two dead, three hospitalized
items.summary: After a suspected overdose in Aurora killed two people and hospitalized three, DEA's Mark Putnam said fentanyl is the most significant drug threat in Colorado and the Denver metro area. DEA reported seizing more than 550 kilograms of fentanyl powder and 3.8 million pills in the state last year, and said the case does not signal a broader trend. Authorities have not named the substances involved, so local naloxone and drug checking messaging remains relevant.

items.headline: Study: fentanyl use is 10% of reported opioid misuse in surveys, yet synthetics are in 91% of opioid deaths
items.summary: Researchers compared 2022-2023 NSDUH responses (n=115,774) with CDC WONDER mortality data and found self-reported fentanyl use of 315 per 100,000 against 3,223 per 100,000 for opioid misuse, while synthetic opioids were involved in 91% of opioid overdose deaths. The implied ratio was 7.0 deaths per 100 people reporting fentanyl use, higher for men and for non-Hispanic Black respondents. The authors caution the ratios are ecological, not individual-level risk, but conclude surveys capture only part of fentanyl exposure, which supports adding toxicology and wastewater surveillance.

items.headline: Mississippi opioid settlement council approves about $39 million in recommendations amid scoring concerns
items.summary: The Mississippi Opioid Settlement Fund Advisory Council settled on roughly $39 million in top 2026 funding recommendations after receiving 149 applications from 120 organizations, which an outside firm, the Steadman Group, scored. Members raised the roughly $14 million in lower-scored state agency applications to the top tier, and several said they had not reviewed the firm's notes or its reasoning. One member noted the firm did not ask whether applicants allow patients to continue prescribed addiction medications, a requirement the council adopted last year, so funding oversight remains a live issue for treatment providers.

items.headline: Ohio health centers install 70 wall-mounted naloxone kits as Cuyahoga County flags a spike in overdose deaths
items.summary: The Centers, which operates five federally qualified health centers in northern Ohio, is placing 70 ONEbox stations above defibrillators, each holding two naloxone doses, gloves, a rescue-breathing mask and a tab-activated instructional video in English and Spanish. The rollout follows a Cuyahoga County Medical Examiner alert citing 40 suspected overdose deaths in October and November, most with cocaine on preliminary screens and about half also involving fentanyl. Because naloxone does not reverse cocaine toxicity on its own, the pattern is a reminder that stimulant-involved deaths need responses beyond opioid-focused kits.

items.headline: Chatham-Kent, Ontario reports 40 suspected overdose deaths through October, about 2.5 times last year
items.summary: Chatham-Kent Public Health says 40 residents died of suspected drug overdoses from Jan 1 to Oct 31, with a rate of 34.7 per 100,000 compared with 14.2 in Ontario. Paramedics logged 295 suspected opioid overdose calls in the first 10 months, up from 135 a year earlier, including 31 in October, while emergency department visits for suspected opioid overdoses fell to 14 from 21 in September. The divergence between EMS calls and ED visits shows why a single surveillance measure can understate community burden.
